findings.title: Task 2.3's model clause for Step by step names no `/orbit:architect`, so the check would read `/orbit:new` first
findings.recommendation: The walk listed `docs/workflows.md` › `### Step by step` and gave task 2.3 the model clause "After an architect session declares the work, …". The start-sections check counts only a `/orbit:<id>` mention or a fenced `<id> ──►` (specs/orbit-user-docs/spec.md:9-11); "an architect session" is neither, and the section's next start command is `/orbit:new` (docs/workflows.md:37), so a page written to the model clause fails task 3.1. The red run catches it, so nothing ships wrong, but the task's own example contradicts the requirement it serves. Make the clause name the command: "After `/orbit:architect <program>` declares the work, …".

findings.title: Task 2.2 says to renumber after adding step 0, then fixes the closing step as `### 8.`
findings.recommendation: getting-started numbers its steps `### 1. Explore` … `### 7. Archive` (docs/getting-started.md:15-103). Task 2.2 adds "step 0", says "renumber", and the walk added "a closing step after Archive (`### 8. Ratify the stage`" (design.md's new decision repeats `### 8.`). With step 0 kept as `### 0.`, no renumber is needed and the closing step is 8; if "renumber" shifts the existing steps up, Archive becomes 8 and the closing step 9. Drop "renumber" from task 2.2 (step 0 is `### 0. Architect`, the existing steps keep their numbers), so the task and design.md agree on `### 8.`.

The residual diff from the fresh pass's commit touches only files in the walk's edit record, and strict validate stays clean apart from the four undeclared new scenarios apply tags.
